name: MenuStrip
purpose: A MenuStrip is the menu bar of a window. It holds top-level menus (File, Edit, View...) and their drop-down items, with shortcut keys and checkmarks.
whenToUse: Give the application a standard menu bar with commands grouped by topic.
Provide keyboard shortcuts for commands.
Expose many commands without cluttering the form.
realWorldExamples: The File, Edit, View, Help menu bar of a text editor.
A View menu with checkable options such as 'Show status bar'.
A Recent Files submenu.
defaultAppearance: A thin bar docked to the top of the form listing menu names in the system font. Clicking an item opens a drop-down; items can have shortcut text, check marks and images.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating a MenuStrip but not assigning it to Form.MainMenuStrip.
commonMistakes.fix: Set Form.MainMenuStrip so Alt-key access and MDI merging work correctly.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting the & before a letter and having no keyboard access.
commonMistakes.fix: Write '&File' to make Alt+F open the menu.

commonMistakes.mistake: Setting ShortcutKeys and also handling KeyDown, which runs the command twice.
commonMistakes.fix: Let the menu item handle the shortcut and remove the extra key code.

relatedNotes.name: ContextMenuStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A pop-up menu that appears on right-click instead of a permanent bar.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A bar of buttons for common commands, usually with icons.

relatedNotes.name: StatusStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A bar at the bottom for status information, not commands.

name: ContextMenuStrip
purpose: A ContextMenuStrip is a pop-up menu that appears when the user right-clicks a control, offering commands that apply to that control or the item under the mouse.
whenToUse: Offer commands such as Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename or Delete for a control.
Add actions for a list item, a tray icon or a custom surface.
Hide less common commands until needed.
realWorldExamples: Right-clicking a file in a list to see Open, Rename, Delete.
Right-clicking the tray icon to show Open and Exit.
Right-clicking a text box to get Cut, Copy and Paste.
defaultAppearance: A small vertical menu with a border that pops up near the mouse pointer. It is not visible on the form until shown, and shows items with optional icons, shortcuts and separators.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating the menu and never attaching it.
commonMistakes.fix: Assign it to the control's ContextMenuStrip property, or call Show(control, location) yourself.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not knowing which control opened the menu when it is shared.
commonMistakes.fix: Read ContextMenuStrip.SourceControl in the item's Click handler.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving menu items enabled that do not apply.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the Opening event to enable, disable or hide items based on the current state.

relatedNotes.name: MenuStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A permanent menu bar at the top of the window.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A permanent bar of buttons, always visible.

relatedNotes.name: NotifyIcon
relatedNotes.difference: Tray icon whose right-click menu is usually a ContextMenuStrip.

name: ToolStrip
purpose: A ToolStrip is a toolbar that holds buttons, labels, combo boxes, separators and other items for quick access to common commands.
whenToUse: Provide quick access to the most used commands.
Show icons with optional text for actions like New, Open and Save.
Host small controls such as a search box or zoom selector.
realWorldExamples: The New/Open/Save toolbar in an editor.
A formatting toolbar with Bold, Italic and font choices.
A browser-like toolbar with Back, Forward and an address box.
defaultAppearance: A slim bar docked to the top (below the MenuStrip) with a drag grip on the left. Items are laid out left to right; items that do not fit move to an overflow arrow on the right.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding controls like Button or TextBox directly.
commonMistakes.fix: Use ToolStrip items (ToolStripButton, ToolStripTextBox, ToolStripComboBox) or wrap a control in ToolStripControlHost.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buttons that show no image and have no text.
commonMistakes.fix: Set DisplayStyle to Text, Image or ImageAndText, and provide an Image or Text.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not setting ToolTipText, which leaves icon-only buttons unexplained.
commonMistakes.fix: Set ToolTipText on each icon button.

relatedNotes.name: MenuStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A text menu bar with drop-downs rather than a row of buttons.

relatedNotes.name: StatusStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A bar for information at the bottom of the window.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStripButton
relatedNotes.difference: The most common item that you place on a ToolStrip.

relatedNotes.name: BindingNavigator
relatedNotes.difference: A ToolStrip with built-in buttons to move through data records.

name: StatusStrip
purpose: A StatusStrip is a bar at the bottom of the window that shows the application's state: messages, progress, counts, the current position or the time.
whenToUse: Show short messages like 'Ready' or 'Saved'.
Display progress or record counts next to the work area.
Present the current mode, zoom level or cursor position.
realWorldExamples: 'Line 12, Col 4' in a code editor.
A 'Ready' message with a progress bar in a download manager.
A connection status indicator in a chat client.
defaultAppearance: A thin bar docked to the bottom of the form, with items starting on the left and a size-grip at the bottom-right corner (SizingGrip = true).

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding a Label or ProgressBar directly to the StatusStrip.
commonMistakes.fix: Use ToolStripStatusLabel and ToolStripProgressBar items.

commonMistakes.mistake: Text is cut off or the label does not stretch.
commonMistakes.fix: Set Spring = true on one label so it fills the remaining space.

commonMistakes.mistake: Updating status from a background thread directly.
commonMistakes.fix: Marshal the call to the UI thread with Invoke.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A bar of command buttons; a StatusStrip displays information.

relatedNotes.name: MenuStrip
relatedNotes.difference: A menu bar at the top, for commands.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStripLabel
relatedNotes.difference: Can be used on a ToolStrip, while a StatusStrip uses ToolStripStatusLabel.

relatedNotes.name: ProgressBar
relatedNotes.difference: Host it in a StatusStrip with ToolStripProgressBar.

name: ToolStripButton
purpose: A ToolStripButton is a button item for a ToolStrip. It can show text, an image or both, and it can stay pressed to act as a toggle.
whenToUse: Add commands like Save or Print to a toolbar.
Create toggle buttons such as Bold or Italic with CheckOnClick = true.
Provide icon-based shortcuts to menu commands.
realWorldExamples: Bold, Italic and Underline toggles in a text editor.
Back and Forward buttons in a viewer.
A 'Refresh' icon in a data window.
defaultAppearance: A flat button that shows a hover highlight when the mouse is over it, with a pressed look when clicked or when Checked is true. DisplayStyle is Image by default, so set it to Text or ImageAndText to show a caption.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting to place a ToolStripButton directly on a form.
commonMistakes.fix: It must live inside a ToolStrip (or similar) container.

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating a toggle button and getting no state change.
commonMistakes.fix: Set CheckOnClick = true and read the Checked property.

commonMistakes.mistake: Large images that are scaled badly.
commonMistakes.fix: Set ImageScaling or use icons sized to the ToolStrip's ImageScalingSize.

relatedNotes.name: Button
relatedNotes.difference: A normal form button; a ToolStripButton belongs only on strips.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: The container that hosts the button.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStripLabel
relatedNotes.difference: Displays text and does not look like a button.

name: ToolStripLabel
purpose: A ToolStripLabel is a text or image item for a ToolStrip or StatusStrip. It can also act as a hyperlink.
whenToUse: Caption another item such as a combo box on a toolbar ('Zoom:').
Show short information on a toolbar.
Provide a link in a strip by setting IsLink = true.
realWorldExamples: 'Search:' before a ToolStripTextBox.
A 'Help' link in a toolbar.
The current file name next to buttons.
defaultAppearance: Plain text with no button border or hover effect. When IsLink = true it looks like a blue underlined hyperlink and the cursor changes to a hand.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using it in a StatusStrip and not getting Spring or border options.
commonMistakes.fix: Use ToolStripStatusLabel in a StatusStrip for those features.

commonMistakes.mistake: Looking for a LinkClicked event on a ToolStripLabel that has IsLink = true.
commonMistakes.fix: ToolStripLabel has no LinkClicked event; handle Click and open the address there.

commonMistakes.mistake: Text that does not update.
commonMistakes.fix: Set the Text property, and call it on the UI thread.

relatedNotes.name: Label
relatedNotes.difference: A normal form label; ToolStripLabel only lives in strips.

relatedNotes.name: LinkLabel
relatedNotes.difference: A form control with multiple links, while ToolStripLabel has one optional link.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: The toolbar that hosts the label.

relatedNotes.name: StatusStrip
relatedNotes.difference: Prefer ToolStripStatusLabel for status text.

name: ToolStripComboBox
purpose: A ToolStripComboBox is a combo box item for a ToolStrip, offering a drop-down list of choices directly on the toolbar.
whenToUse: Select zoom, font or a filter from the toolbar.
Offer a list of values without opening a dialog.
Let users type a value or pick one (DropDownStyle).
realWorldExamples: A font family and font-size selector on a formatting toolbar.
A zoom level list in a viewer.
A search scope selector next to a search box.
defaultAppearance: A small combo box embedded in the toolbar with the toolbar's background, showing the current text and a drop-down arrow.

commonMistakes.mistake: Looking for items on the ToolStripComboBox itself.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the Items collection of the ToolStripComboBox; for advanced properties, use its ComboBox property.

commonMistakes.mistake: Handling TextChanged to detect a selection.
commonMistakes.fix: Use SelectedIndexChanged to react to a choice.

commonMistakes.mistake: Combo box width looks wrong.
commonMistakes.fix: Set the Width (and AutoSize = false) to a fixed size that suits the longest item.

relatedNotes.name: ComboBox
relatedNotes.difference: The same drop-down for use on a form rather than a strip.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStrip
relatedNotes.difference: The container that hosts the item.

relatedNotes.name: ToolStripButton
relatedNotes.difference: A toolbar button for a single action.
